songs.title: The Generations of Adam - Genesis 5
songs.intro: From Adam's generations to Noe's birth, this song follows the long line of lives in Genesis 5 and the hope carried through it.

lyric.label: Song adaptation
lyric.text:
[Verse 1 — intimate, spare]
In the image of God, the first faces shone;
male and female, blessed and known.
Adam saw his likeness in a child called Seth—
two hundred thirty years before that breath.
Seven hundred more, with daughters and sons;
nine hundred thirty, and his days were done.

[Chorus — restrained]
Hand to hand, the living flame;
the years fall down, but the names remain.
Dust takes the body, not the song;
the light goes on, the light goes on.

[Verse 2 — the pulse moves forward]
Seth gave Enos a name at two hundred five;
seven hundred seven more with his house alive.
Nine hundred twelve, then he slipped from sight.
Enos raised Cainan at one hundred ninety;
seven hundred fifteen, children around him;
nine hundred five beneath the turning sky.

[Verse 3 — rising guitars, varied cadence]
Cainan at one hundred seventy called Maleleel his son;
seven hundred forty after, the generations ran.
Nine hundred ten, and his long road closed.
Maleleel at one sixty-five gave Jared his name;
seven hundred thirty more, daughters and sons came;
eight hundred ninety-five, then the silence rose.

[Chorus — fuller, not louder than the bridge]
Hand to hand, the living flame;
the years fall down, but the names remain.
One voice fades, another grows;
the light goes on where the river flows.

[Verse 4 — gathering toward Enoch]
Jared saw Enoch at one hundred sixty-two;
eight hundred years more, and the family grew.
Nine hundred sixty-two: the earth received his breath.
But Enoch was not another line that ended in death.

[Bridge — poignant crescendo, drums and harmony opening]
At one hundred sixty-five, Mathusala came;
two hundred years Enoch walked with God,
with sons and daughters beside his name.
Three hundred sixty-five, and the count stopped there—
he pleased the Lord; he was no longer found.
God translated him beyond the ground.
[Hold the final phrase; let the band crest, then fall to one pulse]

[Verse 5 — grounded again]
Mathusala gave Lamech life at one hundred sixty-seven;
eight hundred two years more beneath the heavens,
sons and daughters, a house grown wide.
Nine hundred sixty-nine, and Mathusala died.
Lamech held a child at one hundred eighty-eight;
five hundred sixty-five more while the family grew.
Seven hundred fifty-three, and his labor was through.

[Final build — a new, warmer crescendo]
His hands knew the soil, and the soil knew pain;
he named the child Noah in hope of rest:
“From our work and the toil of our hands,
from this cursed ground, may comfort come.”
Five hundred years, and Noah’s house rang out:
Shem, Ham and Japeth—three names in the dawn.

[Final chorus — glorious, hopeful, unresolved ending]
Hand to hand, the living flame;
the years fall down, but the names remain.
From weary hands a promise comes;
the light goes on, the light goes on.
Shem, Ham and Japeth—carry it on.

verses.text: This [is] the genealogy of men in the day in which God made Adam; in the image of God he made him:
male and female he made them, and blessed them; and he called his name Adam, in the day in which he made them.
And Adam lived two hundred and thirty years, and begot [a son] after his [own] form, and after his [own] image, and he called his name Seth.
And the days of Adam, which he lived after his begetting Seth, were seven hundred years; and he begot sons and daughters.
And all the days of Adam which he lived were nine hundred and thirty years, and he died.
Now Seth lived two hundred and five years, and begot Enos.
And Seth lived after his begetting Enos, seven hundred and seven years, and he begot sons and daughters.
And all the days of Seth were nine hundred and twelve years, and he died.
And Enos lived an hundred and ninety years, and begot Cainan.
And Enos lived after his begetting Cainan, seven hundred and fifteen years, and he begot sons and daughters.
And all the days of Enos were nine hundred and five years, and he died.
And Cainan lived an hundred and seventy years, and he begot Maleleel.
And Cainan lived after his begetting Maleleel, seven hundred and forty years, and he begot sons and daughters.
And all the days of Cainan were nine hundred and ten years, and he died.
And Maleleel lived an hundred and sixty and five years, and he begot Jared.
And Maleleel lived after his begetting Jared, seven hundred and thirty years, and he begot sons and daughters.
And all the days of Maleleel were eight hundred and ninety and five years, and he died.
And Jared lived an hundred and sixty and two years, and begot Enoch:
and Jared lived after his begetting Enoch, eight hundred years, and he begot sons and daughters.
And all the days of Jared were nine hundred and sixty and two years, and he died.
And Enoch lived an hundred and sixty and five years, and begat Mathusala.
And Enoch was well-pleasing to God after his begetting Mathusala, two hundred years, and he begot sons and daughters.
And all the days of Enoch were three hundred and sixty and five years.
And Enoch was well-pleasing to God, and was not found, because God translated him.
And Mathusala lived an hundred and sixty and seven years, and begot Lamech.
And Mathusala lived after his begetting Lamech eight hundred and two years, and begot sons and daughters.
And all the days of Mathusala which he lived, were nine hundred and sixty and nine years, and he died.
And Lamech lived an hundred and eighty and eight years, and begot a son.
And he called his name Noe, saying, This one will cause us to cease from our works, and from the toils of our hands, and from the earth, which the Lord God has cursed.
And Lamech lived after his begetting Noe, five hundred and sixty and five years, and begot sons and daughters.
And all the days of Lamech were seven hundred and fifty-three years, and he died.
And Noe was five hundred years old, and he begot three sons, Sem, Cham, and Japheth.

lyric.label: Song adaptation
lyric.text:
[Verse 1]
As people grew numerous
upon the earth,
daughters were born to them.

The sons of God saw
the daughters of men were beautiful;
they took as wives
whomever they chose.

The Lord God said,
My Spirit will not stay
with these men forever;
they are flesh.
Their days will be
one hundred twenty years.

Giants lived upon the earth
in those days and afterward.
The sons of God came
to the daughters of men;
their children were the giants of old,
men of renown.

[Breakdown]
The Lord God saw wickedness
multiply upon the earth.
Every heart was brooding
over evil without end.

God took it to heart
that He had made mankind;
He pondered it deeply.

God said, I will wipe away
the people I have made,
and cattle, creatures that crawl,
and birds of the sky.
I grieve that I have made them.

[Bridge]
But Noe found grace
before the Lord God.

These are the generations of Noe.
He was a just man,
perfect in his generation,
and pleasing to God.

Noe fathered three sons: 
Shem, Ham and Japheth.

[Build]
The earth was corrupt before God;
it was filled with wrong.

The Lord God looked on the earth
and saw its corruption;
all flesh had corrupted its way.

The Lord God said to Noe,
The end of all men is before Me.
They have filled the earth with wrong;
I will destroy them
and the earth.

[Verse 2]
Make yourself an ark
of square timber,
with rooms inside;
coat it within and without
with pitch.

Make the ark three hundred cubits long,
fifty cubits wide,
and thirty cubits high.

Narrow the ark as you build it;
finish it a cubit above.
Put its door in the side,
and make lower, second
and third stories.

[Climax]
I will bring a flood of water
upon the earth.
All flesh that breathes beneath heaven
will perish;
everything on earth will die.

[Chorus]
But I will establish
My covenant with you.
Enter the ark with your sons,
your wife, and your sons' wives.

[Verse 3]
Bring pairs of every living kind
into the ark with you: 
cattle, creatures that crawl,
and wild beasts.
Feed them there with you,
male and female.

Birds after their kind,
cattle after their kind,
all that crawl after their kind: 
pairs of each will come to you,
male and female, to be fed.

Gather every kind of food
that you eat;
store it for yourself
and for them.

[Outro]
Noe did everything
the Lord God commanded him.
He did it all.

verses.text: And it came to pass when men began to be numerous upon the earth, and daughters were born to them,
that the sons of God having seen the daughters of men that they were beautiful, took to themselves wives of all whom they chose.
And the Lord God said, My Spirit shall certainly not remain among these men for ever, because they are flesh, but their days shall be an hundred and twenty years.

Now the giants were upon the earth in those days; and after that when the sons of God were wont to go in to the daughters of men, they bore [children] to them, those were the giants of old, the men of renown.
And the Lord God having seen that the wicked actions of men were multiplied upon the earth, and that every one in his heart was intently brooding over evil continually,
then God laid it to heart that he had made man upon the earth, and he pondered [it] deeply.
And God said, I will blot out man whom I have made from the face of the earth, even man with cattle, and reptiles with flying creatures of the sky, for I am grieved that I have made them.
But Noe found grace before the Lord God.
And these [are] the generations of Noe. Noe was a just man; being perfect in his generation, Noe was well-pleasing to God.
And Noe begot three sons, Sem, Cham, Japheth.
But the earth was corrupted before God, and the earth was filled with iniquity.
And the Lord God saw the earth, and it was corrupted; because all flesh had corrupted its way upon the earth.
And the Lord God said to Noe, A period of all men is come before me; because the earth has been filled with iniquity by them, and, behold, I destroy them and the earth.
Make therefore for thyself an ark of square timber; thou shalt make the ark in compartments, and thou shalt pitch it within and without with pitch.
And thus shalt thou make the ark; three hundred cubits the length of the ark, and fifty cubits the breadth, and thirty cubits the height of it.
Thou shalt narrow the ark in making it, and in a cubit above thou shalt finish it, and the door of the ark thou shalt make on the side; with lower, second, and third stories thou shalt make it.
And behold I bring a flood of water upon the earth, to destroy all flesh in which is the breath of life under heaven, and whatsoever things are upon the earth shall die.
And I will establish my covenant with thee, and thou shalt enter into the ark, and thy sons and thy wife, and thy sons' wives with thee.

And of all cattle and of all reptiles and of all wild beasts, even of all flesh, thou shalt bring by pairs of all, into the ark, that thou mayest feed them with thyself: male and female they shall be.

Of all winged birds after their kind, and of all cattle after their kind, and of all reptiles creeping upon the earth after their kind, pairs of all shall come in to thee, male and female to be fed with thee.
And thou shalt take to thyself of all kinds of food which ye eat, and thou shalt gather them to thyself, and it shall be for thee and them to eat.
And Noe did all things whatever the Lord God commanded him, so did he.

songs.title: Salt and Light - Matthew 5
songs.intro: Jesus calls his followers to be salt and light in the Sermon on the Mount.

lyric.label: Song adaptation
lyric.text:
[Verse 1]
Blessed are the poor in spirit
Heaven's kingdom belongs to them
Blessed are the ones who mourn
They will find their comfort
Blessed are the gentle
They will inherit the earth
Those who hunger and thirst for righteousness
Will be filled
Mercy will meet the merciful
Pure hearts will see God
Those who make peace will be called God's children
Those who suffer for doing right have the kingdom
When they speak against you because of Me
Rejoice; your reward is in heaven

[Chorus]
You are the salt of the earth
Do not let it lose its taste
You are the light for the world
A city on a hill cannot hide
No one lights a lamp to cover it
Set it where the whole house can see
Let your good works shine before others
And give your Father glory

[Verse 2]
Do not think I came to tear down the Law
Or the words the prophets gave
I came to bring them to fulfillment
Not one small mark will fall away
Before all is accomplished
You heard the command against murder
I tell you anger also faces judgment
When you bring your gift to the altar
And remember your brother's grievance
Leave your gift and go make peace
Then come and offer it

[Chorus]
You are the salt of the earth
Do not let it lose its taste
You are the light for the world
A city on a hill cannot hide
No one lights a lamp to cover it
Set it where the whole house can see
Let your good works shine before others
And give your Father glory

[Verse 3]
You heard the command against adultery
I tell you lust can sin within the heart
If your right eye leads you into sin
Tear it out and throw it away
Better to lose one part of you
Than your whole body be cast into hell
You heard the command against false vows
But let your yes be yes
And let your no be no

[Bridge]
You heard an eye for an eye
But I tell you, turn the other cheek
If someone takes your coat
Give your cloak as well
If you are forced to walk one mile
Go with them another
Give to the one who asks
Do not turn away the one who needs to borrow

[Outro]
You heard, love your neighbor and hate your enemy
But I tell you, love your enemies
Pray for the ones who persecute you
Your Father sends sunlight on evil and good
And rain on the just and unjust
If you love only those who love you
What reward is there?
Be perfect, as your Father in heaven is perfect
